source.title: Dead-Direction Conditioners: Gauge-Equivariant Preconditioning for Deep Networks

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures train/test generalization on modular-arithmetic grokking tasks, but changes the optimizer and studies gauge-equivariant preconditioning rather than reproducing the original training recipe.
record.gate_note: The paper reports explicit delayed train/test behavior on a modular-addition testbed and reports grokking outcomes under several optimizer and weight-decay conditions. Its language-model results concern overtraining and validation performance, not a reported delayed-generalization jump. The paper does not sweep training-set size.
record.test_reason: Grokking is mainly a benchmark for the DDC optimizer, so most grokking rows compare the authors' own method with baselines. Some results still bear on the claim. The one-block mod-113 testbed reproduces the memorise-then-grok delay (Fig. 23). Vanilla Muon baselines on deeper RoPE transformers grok only partially. Giving vanilla Muon more weight decay speeds grokking, and so does higher weight decay across the AdamW tuning grid. These results bear on V1 (new optimizers and depths) and weakly on V5. The language-model run studies over-training collapse, not delayed generalization, so V4 is not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct but narrow. The authors conclude that gauge-equivariant preconditioning (DDC) holds the optimizer on the symmetry quotient. This makes the singular-learning rate readable (32 vs 7 of 65 cells on an LM) and changes the minimum reached: less degenerate on grokking benches, less over-training collapse on an LM, lower validation loss on a ViT. On grokking, they attribute Muon-base speed-ups to bundled weight decay and credit the projection with reliability (10/11 vs 0/11 seeds at depth 24) and a cleaner axis-aligned dead basis.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses modular-addition grokking tasks and train/test outcomes, but studies DDC gauge projections and Adam/Muon optimizer variants rather than reproducing the original optimizer and training recipe. It also includes language-model and vision experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Grokking outcomes vary with optimizer, depth, activation, rotation-gauge choice (generic rotation versus RoPE-matched torus), and weight-decay matching. No training-set-size sweep is reported.

fits_no_version.finding: Grokking reliability and final accuracy at depth depend on whether the optimizer respects attention-rotation symmetry: gauge arms grok 10/11 seeds at depth 24 vs 0/11 for vanilla Muon.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Whether delayed generalization completes depends on optimizer symmetry handling (gauge-equivariant preconditioning), independent of weight-decay matching.

fits_no_version.finding: On a 75M LM over-trained on 10M tokens, AdamW memorises and validation collapses, while DDCAdam keeps a small train-validation gap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer symmetry handling changes over-training collapse in small LMs (not a grokking claim).

record.problems: The training-set-size dependence in V1 is not tested. Many grokking cohorts use 3 seeds, and the study reports no delayed-generalization result on realistic language data; its language-model results are overtraining comparisons instead.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows were retained for non-grokking geometry, gauge-mode drift, or vision compression results because they do not measure the delayed-generalization behavior named by the tested versions. The language-model overtraining metrics relevant to V4 are included in r17–r18.

untested.parts: Dependence of the delay on training-set size; the split is fixed at 30%.
Entire version: no circuit formation or progress measures anticipating the jump.
Entire version: no delayed generalization on non-algorithmic data, and no sweep of initialization scale or lazy-to-rich regime.
Entire version: the LM run measures over-training collapse, not grokking-like delayed generalization.
Critical dataset size, ungrokking below it, and the circuit-efficiency mechanism itself.
Entire version: optimizer variants are compared, but adaptive-optimizer instability or softmax floating-point limits are not tested as causes of the delay.

missing.what: Per-optimizer lr × WD grid. AdamW grok step falls with weight decay (8200/4100/2200 at lr 1e-3) and AdamW fails to grok in the low-lr corner. SGD groks only in a low-WD band that narrows as effective shrinkage rises. Muon groks at every grid point.
Width sweep d_model ∈ {128, 64, 32}: grokking fails at the d32 'near-cliff' size (model size, not dataset size).
Strong Z-loss (alpha = 1) under AdamW prevents grokking.
Plain Muon at depth 8 in the curvature cohort groks 0/3 seeds (0.848); recorded only as r10's baseline.

record.verdict_notes: Primarily an optimizer paper that uses the Nanda et al. modular-addition testbed. Only baseline (vanilla) arms and the weight-decay control bear on the claim; the gauge arms are method performance. V4 was relabelled as not tested: the LM experiment never looks for delayed generalization, so the reader's 'challenges' label and the 'reversed' state on r17 were removed. The V5 limits_scope label on r15 was removed because r15 is a method comparison. Grokking trials mostly use 3 seeds without error bars on grok steps.

versions.untested_parts: The effect of shrinking the training set on the optimization delay was not tested; the main one-block task uses a fixed 30% training split.
The study does not trace formation of a Fourier or other identifiable generalizing circuit against memorizing components, or test whether continuous progress measures anticipate a test-accuracy jump.
The vision-transformer experiment reports compression and validation performance, not delayed generalization; initialization-scale or lazy-to-rich transitions are not tested.
The study tests one small language model trained on a FineWeb-edu slice, not fine-tuning or larger realistic-model training. It does not report a delayed generalization jump in that run.

The study tests weight decay's contribution to grokking speed and reliability, but not a critical dataset size, ungrokking below that size, or the proposed low-norm-versus-memorization efficiency mechanism as a whole.
No comparison identifies whether runs converge to the same algorithm across architectures or hyperparameters.
The study does not test adaptive-optimizer instability or floating-point/softmax limits as explanations for grokking.

relationships.reason: Train accuracy memorises by step 200; validation stays at chance for thousands of steps, then groks at steps 4800–5600 (r1).
relationships.display_finding: Training accuracy saturated by step 200, while validation remained at chance for thousands of steps before grokking at steps 4,800–5,600.

source_check.reason: Figure 23 explicitly reports memorization by step 200 followed by validation grokking at steps 4800–5600. Training-set-size dependence is untested.

relationships.condition: Vanilla Muon on deeper RoPE modular-arithmetic transformers (depth 8 and 24)
relationships.reason: Plain Muon groks in only 1/3 seeds at depth 8 (0.867) and 0/3 at depth 24, stalling near 0.65–0.78 within 6000 steps. The jump depends on optimizer and depth (r2, r7, r9).
relationships.display_finding: Within 6,000 steps, depth 8 grokked in 1/3 seeds with reported accuracy 0.867, while depth 24 grokked in 0/3 and stalled near 0.65–0.78.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Vanilla Muon on deeper RoPE modular-arithmetic transformers (depth 8 and 24)
source_check.reason: Grokking is unreliable at depth 8 (1/3 seeds within 5000 steps) and incomplete at depth 24 (0/3 for each activation within 6000 steps). The label fits these restricted conditions; the verdict reason should distinguish the two training budgets.

relationships.condition: One-block mod-113 transformer, Muon base; also the AdamW tuning grid (text, Fig. 24)
relationships.reason: More weight decay speeds grokking: matched-WD Muon groks at 4120 vs 5080 (r13, r14). Per the text, AdamW at lr 1e-3 groks at 8200/4100/2200 steps for WD 0.5/1/2 (not in rows). Only speed is shown, not a critical dataset size.
relationships.display_finding: More weight decay shortened Muon grokking time from 5,080 to 4,120 steps, while AdamW at learning rate 0.001 grokked at 8,200, 4,100, and 2,200 steps for weight decay 0.5, 1, and 2, respectively.

relation.reason: Although grokking serves as an optimizer benchmark, the study measures the memorization-to-generalization transition, baseline grokking failures, and the effect of increased weight decay.

tranche.reason: The study reports delayed generalization and its reliability in new optimizer and deeper RoPE transformer settings, including vanilla baselines that bear directly on V1 and weight-decay controls bearing on V5.

source_check.notes: Figure 8 includes one-standard-deviation error bars across three seeds. The study tests delayed generalization and decay-dependent acceleration, but does not establish the full dataset-size prediction of V1 or the full efficiency account of V5.

statements.correction: Depth 8, vanilla Muon, weight decay 1.0, 5000 steps, 3 seeds: 1/3 grok, final accuracy 0.867 (Appendix C.7). Depth 24, weight decay 1.0, 6000 steps: vanilla Muon groks 0/3 for each activation; GELU accuracy 0.652, squared-ReLU accuracy 0.783 (Appendix C.6).
statements.problem: The seed counts are correct, but the statement assigns a 6000-step budget to both depths. The depth-8 cohort ran for 5000 steps.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: mod-113 one-block testbed and reported modular-addition grokking cohorts
reader_labels.reason: The one-block task has training memorisation by step 200, chance validation for thousands of steps, and grokking at steps 4800–5600 (r1); multiple modular-addition optimizer settings also reach high final accuracy (r3–r6, r8, r10, r12, r15–r16).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: depth-24 vanilla Muon, for both tested activations
reader_labels.reason: Vanilla Muon reaches only partial final accuracy and none of the three seeds meet the paper's grokking threshold for GELU or squared-ReLU (r7, r9); results therefore depend on optimizer and setting.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: the tested 12-layer language model trained on a 10-million-token FineWeb-edu slice
reader_labels.reason: The reported AdamW run overfits and validation collapses, while DDCAdam holds lower train accuracy and improves final validation metrics; neither result is a reported delayed generalization jump (r17–r18).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: weight-decay-matched Muon comparison on the mod-113 task
reader_labels.reason: Increasing vanilla Muon's weight decay to match the gauge's effective shrinkage changes its grok step from 5080 to 4120, close to the gauge's 4160, supporting a contribution of weight decay to grokking speed (r12–r14).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: matched nominal weight decay on the mod-113 task
reader_labels.reason: At equal nominal weight decay the paper attributes the gauge's remaining advantage to grokking reliability, not speed; the study does not establish the proposed low-norm efficiency mechanism or its critical-size and ungrokking predictions (r15).
